source_evidence: Institutional Shares (Class I) may have some of the lowest ongoing operating expenses, but there could be relatively high initial investment minimums and/or transaction fees to invest directly through a brokerage account.
answer: Institutional Shares, also called Class I, may have some of a mutual fund’s lowest ongoing operating expenses. However, investing directly through a brokerage account could involve a high initial minimum or transaction fees. Some funds also make Class I shares available to retail investors through an employer retirement plan or an investment advisory account. Because availability and costs can differ, compare the fees and expenses that apply to each share class rather than assuming Class I is always the least expensive overall.
